source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New Jersey has mapped 48 data center facilities but only five publish power capacity, and CyrusOne's Totowa NYM2 is one of the five, at 6 MW of IT load.

The pattern is a disclosure gap rather than a capacity gap. Forty-eight facilities are mapped in the state, five carry a published power figure, and those five total 111.3 MW. NYM2's 6 MW is 5.4 percent of that published total and ranks fourth of the five, which places it in the middle of the only facilities in New Jersey whose compute scale can actually be measured. The 200,000 square feet of technical space against 6 MW works out to roughly 30 watts per square foot, and the data offers no second facility to compare that density against.

For AI specifically, the published number is the whole story and it is small. At 40 kW per rack, 6 MW of IT load implies about 150 racks, and the operator does not break that down by workload or accelerator type. The record contains no power distribution architecture, no cooling capacity, and no grid connection detail, so it cannot say whether this campus is limited by its utility feed or by its own thermal design. SSAE 16 Type II is an audit of security and availability controls, not a statement about compute.

What the data does not cover matters here. The suitability score of 52 is built from published IT capacity and operator type, and it lists announced expansion as missing, so nothing here indicates whether CyrusOne intends to grow the site. The record carries no address and no coordinates, so proximity to transmission or substation capacity cannot be assessed. The 111.3 MW statewide figure is a floor set by voluntary disclosure, not a measure of New Jersey's actual data center load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
